ON BIRD-CATCHING.

You will carry a dog’s tongue hidden in your shoe under your big toe, or if you carry a dried dog’s heart with you, according to Sextus; or hare’s hair or dung, according to Pliny. Or you will carry the severed tail of a young weasel on your foot, or you will give it a frog in a morsel of food; all these things are for avoiding the barking of dogs. Nigidius says that dogs flee from the sight of a man all day if he expels a tick from a dog and carries it for a while. Oppianus:

> *But if you carry a small piece of a hyena’s skin*
> *That has been cut off, immediately the puppies and the fierce dogs*
> *Will be struck with bitter terror, and they will not bark at you*
> *As you walk by, even if they were barking before.*

### *So that a dog cannot run.*

If you smear its wings with oil, it will be hindered in its running; this will happen in this way.

### *So that a hawk may be spirited.*

You will animate the bird against its prey so that it attacks large birds. Moisten the food it uses during the hunting season with wine, or if it is a goshawk, give it a little vinegar. When you want it to fly, give it three morsels of meat moistened with wine, or pour wine into the beak of a dove chick, then make it fly. Thus:

### *You will make partridges more combative,*

If you give them sprigs of maidenhair fern <term>adiantum</term> <gloss>a type of fern</gloss> in their food, according to Pliny. And:

### *Roosters become more combative,*

By giving them garlic in their food when they are about to fight. From this, in an old comedy, they are very wittily called <term>eskorodismenoi</term> <gloss>garlic-stuffed</gloss>, that is, fed with garlic, for one who is vehement and too prone to fighting.

### *So that a bird does not fly high,*

Pluck out the tail feathers that direct its course upward; thus it will fly in a circle below. If you wish:

### *So that a bird cannot fly,*

Cut the upper and lower tendons of the wing, and it remains without harm; the bird will not fly, and in this way, they do not escape in aviaries.

<summary>This page provides various folk remedies and "natural magic" techniques for hunters, including methods to silence barking dogs, increase the aggression of hawks and roosters, and physically prevent birds from flying or flying high.</summary>
<keywords>hunting, bird-catching, animal behavior, folk medicine, Pliny, Oppianus, Nigidius, hawks, roosters, partridges</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page: Each one</meta> is distinguished by piety, religion, prudence, and the worship and veneration of God, as if perceived by the eyes of true reason, and by the confidence of his own belief, he excels among men as much as the sun surpasses the other stars in its light. For the sun itself illuminates the other stars not so much by the magnitude of its divinity as by its holiness. Believe, O Asclepius, that this is the second god, governing all things and illuminating all worldly living beings, whether animate or inanimate. For if the world is a living being that always was, is, and will be, nothing in the world is mortal. For of every living part that is in the world, just as in one and the same animal that is always living, there is no place for mortality. Therefore, God himself must be most full of life and eternity, if it is necessary for him to live always. Therefore, just as the world is eternal, so the sun itself is always the governor of vital things, or the frequent visitor and dispenser of all their vitality. Therefore, God is the eternal governor of the living, or of the vital things that are in the world, and the eternal dispenser of life itself. He has dispensed it once by an eternal law, granting life to all vital things in the manner which I shall describe.

<summary>This passage identifies the sun as the second god and the eternal governor of all living things within the world, emphasizing that the world and its vital components are inherently immortal under divine law.</summary>
<keywords>Asclepius, Sun, second god, eternal law, vitality, immortality, world-soul, divine governance</keywords>

Varro testifies that he has seen these. And there are things more wonderful than these: for on the Attic shore, the sea sounds like a cithara. At Megara, a certain rock, when struck, produces the sound of a stringed instrument; so great is the power of music. It soothes the soul, elevates the mind, incites combatants to war, and lightens the labors and fatigue of individual tasks. It recalls the fallen and the desperate, and comforts travelers. And the Arabs say that camels carrying burdens are comforted by the singing of their guides. In a similar way, those carrying heavy loads sing, and are made capable and relieved by it: for song produces delight and capability, mitigates the irascible, gladdens the sad and anxious, pacifies the discordant, and dissipates vain thoughts. Hence it is that Democritus and Theophrastus affirm that certain diseases of the body and mind can be cured or induced in this way. Thus we read that Terpander and Arion of Methymna <note>original: "Methymnæum"</note>

For the good is innate to truth, together with life and light, and no avenger has come to go beyond it. Indeed, all the avenging powers were cast out by a certain sudden impulse. You have understood, my son, the manner of regeneration itself. The intellectual generation is composed by the presence of the number ten, which rejects the number twelve. And we have contemplated this from the generation itself. Whoever, therefore, because of the kindness of the generation which is according to God, loses his bodily sense, knows himself to be composed of divine things. Having become uninclined <note>meaning: no longer drawn toward material or base things</note>, he rejoices in the divine power with his whole mind. **TATIUS.** O father, I conceive this not by the intuition of the eyes, but by the act of the mind, which is exercised through the inner powers. I am in heaven, in earth, in water, in air. I am in animals, in trees, in the body, before the body, and after the body. But I would have you tell me further, how the avenging shadows are repelled by the ten powers from the number twelve. What is the method, Trismegistus? **TRISM.** This tabernacle, O son, is constituted from the zodiacal circle, which consists of that number twelve. And the numbers are eleven, and one which is omniform according to the ideas of nature, for the wandering and circuit of man. Therefore, those avenging powers are in a way separated from one another, yet in acting they are in a way joined, as for example, recklessness is inseparable from wrath. Rightly, therefore, according to correct reason, they are separated insofar as they are repelled by the ten powers, that is, by the number ten. The number ten, O son, is the generator of the soul. But life...

<keywords>regeneration, zodiac, number ten, number twelve, intellectual generation, soul, divine power, Trismegistus</keywords>

Therefore, the gods are the princes of all species; these are followed by the gods whose prince is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence/substance</gloss>. These are sensible, of both origins, and similar to one another, who accomplish all things through sensible nature. Each one illuminates its own work through the other. The heaven, or whatever is encompassed by that name, has as its <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>prince of essence</gloss> Jupiter. For through the heaven, Jupiter offers life to all things. The <term>ousiarches</term> of the sun is light. For the good of light is infused into us through the orb of the sun. Of the thirty-six stars <note>original: "xxxvi"</note> (whose name is Horoscopij <note>original: "Horoscopij"</note>) that are always fixed in the same place, their <term>ousiarches</term> or prince is he whom they call <term>Pantomorphon</term> <gloss>all-formed</gloss> or Omniform. He who makes diverse forms for diverse species. The seven spheres that are called erratic have <term>ousiarchas</term> <gloss>princes of essence</gloss>, that is, their own princes, which they call fortune, <term>eimarmenēs</term> <gloss>fate</gloss>, by which all things are changed, by the law of nature with the firmest stability, and varied by eternal agitation. The air, indeed, is the organ or machine of all things, through which all things are made. Moreover, he is the second <term>ousiarches</term> of this, for mortals, mortal things, and things similar to these. Therefore, with these things being so, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things pertaining to themselves are naturally connected in such a way that mortal things are annexed to mortal things, and sensible things to sensible things. But the sum of governance obeys that highest Lord, so that they are not many, or rather, they are one. For all things depend from the one, and flow down from it rather, when they are seen at a distance, they are believed to be many, divided. But when united, they are one, or rather two: from whence all things are made, and by whom they are made. That is, from the matter of which they are made, and from his will, by whose nod other things are effected. ASCLEPIUS: This is again the reason, O Trismegistus. TRISMEGISTUS: Such it is, O Asclepius. For God, either as father or lord...

Indeed, arsenic certainly cannot be fixed at all, unless the operating artist has an equal knowledge of its coloring spirit, in which matter all the philosophers have slumbered, attempting in vain to effect anything from it. Whoever, therefore, is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing it, nor of attributing to it the virtue by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening of which mention has been made is derived from a false foundation, and that by it copper is falsely whitened, not transmuted. The Sophists, having masked and disguised Venus <note>the alchemical term for copper</note> in this manner, mixed it with double its weight of Luna <note>the alchemical term for silver</note>, sold it to goldsmiths and moneyers; and finally, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters, not only those who sold it, but also those who bought it. Some of the Sophists, in place of white, took red arsenic, and this itself resulted in a false art. For in whatever way it may be prepared, it exhibits nothing but whiteness. Some have proceeded further, to common sulfur, which they cooked with vinegar, lye, or very sharp urines for a day and a night, until it emerged white. Afterward, they elevated it from common salt and eggshells, cooked and sublimated it through sublimation, and that many times; nevertheless, it remained always combustible, although white: yet, by this means, to fix raw mercu<column-break/>ry...

<summary>The author continues his critique of "sophistic" alchemical practices, specifically condemning the use of arsenic and sulfur to create false whitening effects on copper, which he labels as fraudulent and ineffective for true transmutation.</summary>
<keywords>arsenic, Venus, copper, Luna, silver, Sophists, counterfeiters, sulfur, sublimation, fixation, transmutation</keywords>

where they should have taken <term>pyrites</term> <gloss>a metallic mineral</gloss>, <term>sulphur</term>, <term>salt</term>, <term>metal</term>, and various other materials, they took instead substances in which there is no operation. Although these things are expensive in the shops, they are of no value at all in the work. Our material, however, is not bought in any shop, yet it is found there daily, and merchants throw it into the streets. It is sufficient, therefore, that it be found for free. But the material of our <term>stone</term> is compared to all those things with which the artisans labor. For our stone is our <term>salt</term>, our <term>Mercury</term>, <term>verdigris</term>, <term>saltpeter</term>, <term>sal ammoniac</term>, <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>, <term>sulphur</term>, and infinite other things of this kind, yet not dug from wild, rural mountains with hammers and other tools. But our stone is extracted solely from our own mountains and springs. In our <term>Salt-spring</term> our <term>Salt</term> is found. From our earth our metal, <term>Mercury</term>, and <term>sulphur</term> are cast, and not from wild, foreign, or rural mountains, which the artisans do not understand, nor can they believe or comprehend. For the Lord has obscured and closed their senses, for which reason they used these things otherwise than they ought to have been used, and they did not aim at the target at all. Nevertheless, they persisted in this contrary sense and followed their own stubborn heads. For when they should have <term>distilled</term> gently, they <term>sublimed</term> with a strong fire; they scorched the <term>aqua fortis</term> <gloss>strong water/nitric acid</gloss>, and they immediately burned the operation of nature and the substances themselves, reducing them to nothing. When they should have <term>dissolved</term>, they <term>coagulated</term> instead, and again, like those unskilled in things, they handled the matter unskillfully and fell into doubt. They kept saying with lying words that the art is not true but false, in which, however, they rightly lie. For their own ignorance shamefully deceived them, which must be imputed to their own dark and murky cunning, while, according to their own obscure intellect, they interpreted words otherwise than they sounded. For example, when the Philosophers spoke of <term>calcining</term> (which they call grinding), those unskilled <term>Philosophasters</term> <gloss>pseudo-philosophers</gloss> understood it as burning, and they reduced the things entirely to ashes, so that nothing could be made from them. Also, when the Philosophers <term>dissolve</term>, or transmute into water, those <term>nasutuli</term> <gloss>conceited/nosy ones</gloss> burned the nature with <term>aqua fortis</term>, and the same water, which has no power in

<meta>continues from previous page: ...the time</meta> requires the temperance of fire, and the succession of that increase little by little, with caution, until it is fixed in its lime, so that it may not easily return into a body, so that a greater fire may be administered to it, for the perfection of its lime. Similarly, let him not happen to err in <term>Jupiter</term> <gloss>tin</gloss>, because of the difficulty of its reduction, so that if at any time he places its lime into reduction, it happens to him that it does not reduce, but he finds it of its former disposition or reduced into glass, and he deems its reduction impossible. For we say that if he does not apply a great fire in the reduction of <term>Jupiter</term>, it will not reduce. But if he applies a great one, it does not necessarily happen that it reduces, but it is possible that it reduces it into vitrification. And that is because <term>Jupiter</term> has a fugitive substance of <term>argentum vivum</term> <gloss>quicksilver/mercury</gloss> included in the depth of its nature. Which, if it draws out a long delay in the fire, will flee, and will leave the body deprived of humidity, so that it is found to be converted more apt for vitrification than for the fusion of a metallic body. For everything deprived of its own humidity gives no fusion except a vitrifying one. And therefore it is necessarily left that, with the most rapid impetus of fire, he hastens to reduce it quickly. For otherwise it is not reduced. Let him therefore practice at that, and he will know.

The second mode of calcination of these two bodies, <term>Saturn</term> <gloss>lead</gloss> and <term>Jupiter</term> <gloss>tin</gloss>, which is perfected by the sharpness of salt, is that a quantity of salt be thrown upon their face, quantity after quantity very often in their fusion, and be mixed by much agitation through an iron rod, over the fire, until they are turned into ash through the mixture of salt. And afterwards, let their lime be perfected by the same mode of perfection, with its considerations. But in this there is also a difference in the calcination of these two bodies. Because <term>plumbum</term> <gloss>lead</gloss> is converted to powder from the first labors of calcination more easily than <term>Jupiter</term>, yet its lime is not perfected more easily than that of <term>Jupiter</term>. The cause of this depends on the fact that <term>Saturn</term> has a more fixed humidity than <term>Jupiter</term>.

829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a person, and from those highest parts their lower parts live and shine, and because Mohammed is present in their minds together with their religion, therefore some Mohammed is always placed in their view. And so that they may turn their faces toward the East, upon which the Lord is, he is placed below the Christian center. It is not Mohammed himself, who wrote the <term>Alcoranum</term> <gloss>Koran</gloss>, but another who performs his office; nor is it always the same one, but he is changed. Once it was a man from Saxony who, having been captured by the Algerians, became a Mohammedan. Because he had also been a Christian, he was sometimes moved to speak with them about the Lord, that He was not the son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Others have succeeded this Mohammed later. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like a torch, so that he may be recognized; but that fire is not visible to any others than the Mohammedans.

830. Mohammed himself, who wrote the <term>Alcoranum</term>, does not come into view today. It was told to me that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over all things of their religion as a god, he was cast out from his seat, which he had held under the Catholics, and was sent down to the right side near the south. Once, a certain society of Mohammedans was stirred up by malicious persons to acknowledge Mohammed as God. In order that the sedition might be quieted, Mohammed was brought up from the lower earth and shown, and then he was also seen by me. He appeared like those corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, with a face tending toward black, and I heard him speaking these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and soon he seemed to subside.

831. The Mohammedans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith of three Divine Persons, and thence the worship of three Gods, as many Creators; and furthermore, toward the Roman Catholics because of their genuflections before images, and thence they call the latter idolaters and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they say one but mutter three, and therefore that they divide Omnipotence, and from one and of one make three; and that they are thus like fauns with three horns, one for each god, and together three for one, and that they pray thus, chant thus, and sound thus from their pulpits.

832. The Mohammedans, like all nations that acknowledge one God, and love what is just, and do good from religion, have their own Heaven, but outside the Christian one. However, the Mohammedan Heaven is divided into two. In the lower one, they live honestly with several wives, but from there no others are raised into the higher Heaven than those who renounce concubines, and acknowledge the Lord our Savior, and at the same time His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells, because He is the Son of God the Father. This faith is among them, through which ascent into the higher Heaven is given to them by the Lord.

833. That the Mohammedan religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a scandal to those who think about Divine Providence, and at the same time believe that no one can be saved unless they were born a Christian. But the Mohammedan religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these inquire in what it consists, and they also find it. It is in this, that the Mohammedan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made only the <term>Alcoranum</term> the book of their religion, and thence Mohammed, who wrote it, has settled in their thoughts, and they follow him with some worship, they therefore think little about our Lord. In order that it may be fully known that that religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be told in some order, but first about the origin of idolatries. Before that religion, there was idolatrous worship.

<summary>This page describes the spiritual status and placement of Mohammedans, noting their hostility toward the Christian doctrine of the Trinity and their own specific path to salvation through acknowledging the Lord's dominion. It also explains that the Mohammedan religion was permitted by Divine Providence to help eradicate widespread idolatry.</summary>
<keywords>Mohammed, Koran, Divine Providence, Trinity, Idolatry, Spiritual World, Mohammedan Heaven, Salvation</keywords>

ON OCCULT PHILOSOPHY,

### On the images of the head and tail of the Moon's dragon. Chap. XLV.

<note>A woodcut depicts a serpent or dragon coiled into a circular shape resembling the Greek letter Theta (Θ). The creature has the head of a bird (hawk) and a pointed tail. Within the circular body, there is a central vertical line crossed by a shorter horizontal line, with small astrological or symbolic marks at the terminals.</note>

They also used to make an image of the head and tail of the Moon's dragon, specifically the figure of a serpent between an airy and a fiery circle, with the head of a hawk surrounding them, in the likeness of the Greek letter <term>theta</term> <gloss>Θ</gloss>. They made it when Jupiter held the mid-heaven with that head, which image they affirm contributes much to the success of petitions. They wished to signify by that image a good and happy <term>daemon</term> <gloss>spirit</gloss>, and they wished to represent him through the image of a serpent. For the Egyptians and Phoenicians celebrated this as a divine animal above all others, and celebrated its divine nature, because in it, above other animals, there exists a sharper and more ample spirit. This fact is shown both by its swift movement, without any feet or hands or other instruments, and because it repeatedly renews its age and becomes young again with extraordinary ease. They made an image of the tail in a similar way, when the moon was eclipsed in the tail, or was badly affected by Saturn or Mars. They made it to induce anxiety and infirmity, and they called it an evil genius. A certain Hebrew had enclosed such an image in a double golden belt, which Blanche, the daughter of the Duke of Bourbon, gave as a gift to her husband Peter, the first of that name, King of Spain (whether knowingly or unknowingly). When he was girded with it, he seemed to himself to be surrounded by a serpent. Having subsequently discovered the magic power inserted into the belt, he repudiated his wife for that reason.

### On the images of the mansions of the moon. Chap. XLVI.

They also made images in the individual mansions of the Moon. In the first, for the destruction of someone, they made an image in an iron ring of a black man dressed in haircloth and girded, throwing a lance with his right hand; they sealed it in black wax and fumigated it with liquid storax and uttered imprecations. In the second, against the anger of a prince and for his reconciliation, they sealed in white wax and mastic an image of a crowned king, and fumigated it with wood of aloes. In the third, they made an image in a silver ring, the measure of which was square, and the figure of which was a woman well-dressed sitting in a chair, with her right hand raised above her head; they sealed and fumigated it with musk, camphor, and aromatic nail <note>likely referring to the dried operculum of a sea snail, used in incense</note>. They asserted that this grants prosperity of fortune and every good thing. In the fourth, for vengeance and separation, enmity and malevolence, they sealed in red wax an image of a soldier sitting on a horse, holding a serpent in his right hand, and fumigated it with red myrrh and storax. In the fifth, for the favor of kings and officials and a good reception, they sealed from silver the head of a man, and fumigated it with sandalwood. But the unlearned, and even nature itself, from whom the truth did not proceed, have failed to obtain the gifts of the Lord, nor do they have the knowledge of the immortal God. Not listening to both the gods and divine men, they have rejected all the gods, but they have chosen not only not to hate the prohibited demons, but even to revere them. While pretending to worship God, they do not perform the only things through which God is adored. For God, as the Father of all, needs nothing; but it is good for us when we adore him through justice, chastity, and other virtues, making our very life a prayer to him through imitation and instruction from him. For instruction purges the mind, while imitation deifies the affection by working toward him. He preached well that God is the Father, and he said with what morals he should be worshipped. The prophetic books of the Hebrews are full of these precepts, whether the life of the saints is praised or blamed. But it was only among the Christians, or rather, it is slandered as much as the demons—whom they opine to be gods—desire, as if it were difficult for anyone to recall what shameful and disgraceful things were done in the theaters and temples for the sake of the gods, and to attend to what is read, said, and heard in the churches, or what is offered to God, and from this to understand where there is a building up and where there is a ruin of morals. But who said this to him, or inspired him, if not a diabolical spirit, such a vain and fitting lie, that Christians would rather revere than hate the demons whom the Hebrews were forbidden to worship? But that God whom the wise men of the Hebrews worshipped, and whom we, in this our mortal pilgrimage, venerate and love along with the celestial holy angels and the virtues of God, whom we consider most blessed as fellow citizens, forbids sacrifice in the law which he gave to his people, the Hebrews; and he threatened it very menacingly, saying: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be eradicated." And lest anyone should think that it was commanded not to sacrifice to the worst demons and earthly spirits—whom he calls mimes or lesser ones—because they were also called gods in the holy scriptures, not by the Hebrews <column-break/> but by the Gentiles, which the seventy interpreters clearly set down in the psalm, saying: "For all the gods of the Gentiles are demons," lest anyone should therefore think that it was forbidden to sacrifice to these demons, but that it was permitted to sacrifice to the celestial ones, either to all or to some, he immediately added: "except to the Lord alone," that is, except to the Lord only, lest perhaps someone, hearing "to the Lord alone," might think that there is only one God to whom one ought to think sacrifice should be made. That this is not to be understood in that way is very easily found in the Greek scriptures. Therefore, the God of the Hebrews, to whom even this philosopher gives such great testimony, gave a law to his Hebrew people, written in the Hebrew language, not obscure and unknown, but already spread among all the nations, in which law it is written: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be eradicated, except to the Lord only." What need is there in this law of his and in his prophets to search for many things regarding this matter? Indeed, there is no need to search, for they are not hidden or erased, but are open and frequent; I shall collect them and place them in this my disputation, by which it appears clearer than light that the true and supreme God wished to be sacrificed to by no one at all except to himself alone. Behold this one thing, briefly, or rather, grandly, menacingly, but truthfully said by that God whom their most learned men preach: let it be heard, feared, and fulfilled, lest eradication follow the disobedient. "He who sacrifices to gods," he says, "shall be eradicated, except to the Lord only." Not that he needs anything, but because it is expedient for us that we be his. For it is sung to him in the sacred writings of the Hebrews: "I said to the Lord, you are my God, for you do not need my goods." But the most excellent and best sacrifice of this one is we ourselves. This is his city, the mystery of which we celebrate with our offerings, which are known to the faithful, as we have disputed in the preceding books. For the prophets of the Hebrews interpreted that the victims which the Jews offered in the shadow of the future were to cease, and that the nations would offer one sacrifice from the rising of the sun to its setting, just as we now see being done.

The matter in which the Lord God is acknowledged is that they are performed through all the attributes, which are completed by the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy. As you will find in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, in his expulsion, and in all those matters, you will find that they all came about through the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy. Everything is in complete perfection, with Mercy and Justice, all as is appropriate in true judgment. According to this principle, the Torah says, "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: The Rock, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty. He does not decree the judgment except that "His work is perfect," meaning the judgment He decreed was previously deliberated upon by the two attributes, Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness/Grace</gloss> and Justice. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect," for the word "perfect" <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect/whole</gloss> is the secret of two things. It is as if it said "twins" <term>te'umim</term> <gloss>twins</gloss>, but in honorable language, it refers to the two things above as "perfect," and below as "twins." Thus it says, "And they shall be twins" <note>Exodus 26:24</note> below, "they shall be perfect" <note>Exodus 26:24</note> at the top. Below, they are "twins," and above, they are "perfect," because below they appear as two things, a thing and its opposite, like a helper and an accuser. But above, everything is one intent; whether it is the helper or the accuser, both have one intent, and there is no hatred or love there, and no partiality, but only true judgment. Therefore, it says "His work is perfect," for He deliberated in Justice and Mercy and decreed the judgment, and this is the secret of true judgment. Regarding what is said, "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, it means everything is for the eye of every beholder, as it says, "For all His ways are justice." You already know that justice is included in Justice and Mercy, for justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the middle line, the one who mediates between the two tents, which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness, Isaac corresponds to Justice, and Jacob decides between them, "a plain man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on the side of Abraham and from Justice on the side of Isaac. Thus it says, "Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have performed" <note>Psalms 99:4</note>. The prophet said, "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse is: "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice," what he said "but" <term>akh</term> <gloss>but/only</gloss> divides, meaning in half the attribute of justice, which is Loving-kindness, for justice is half Justice and half Loving-kindness. Therefore, he said "but with justice," and said afterwards, "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret to diminish half of the justice from the side of anger. Therefore, justice depends on Jacob, who is the father of the tribes. He knew great sorrow regarding the children when the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed upon them, so he sought for them mercy and righteousness. The secret is, "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written after it? "And the Holy God is sanctified in righteousness" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. This means when the Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice, He rests the Justice and makes room for the attribute of God <term>El</term> <gloss>God (attribute of Mercy)</gloss>, which is the secret of what is said, "And the Holy God is sanctified in righteousness." In general, when the Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice, the attribute of God comes, which is above, and performs righteousness, and the justice is worked. This is the secret of what they said, that justice is included in Loving-kindness and Justice, and it says, "Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have performed." The great secret is, "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" <note>Psalms 89:15</note>, for righteousness is sometimes Justice, according to its reception of the flow, as we explained that righteousness is great Justice in strength. But when justice participates with it, then the throne is established in Mercy. And if He is exalted in justice, and reaches until Loving-kindness and Truth together, they are called the "shining faces," then everything is made into great Mercy, and this is the secret of "They shall precede..."

### **Torah** Light. These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Service, and Acts of Loving-kindness. Torah is the prohibition of "You shall not add and you shall not subtract," <note>Deuteronomy 13:1</note> which indicates the perfection of the Torah. It is as the philosophers said: a thing that is perfect in the ultimate sense of perfection, it is not appropriate to call it lacking or excessive. For if it were lacking, it would not be perfect; and if it were to receive an addition, it would be found that it was not perfect. Therefore, the definition of the perfect is that it contains neither lack nor excess. It is known that the Torah depends on His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term> <gloss>the Tetragrammaton</gloss>, "The Torah of the Lord is perfect," <note>Psalm 19:8</note> as I have elaborated upon this in my tractate <term>Shevuot</term> <gloss>Oaths</gloss>, in my chapter "Torah Light." And as it is written in the <term>Zohar</term> <gloss>Book of Splendor</gloss> regarding the verse, "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: <term>Yod-He</term> with "My name" equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>. <term>Vav-He</term> with "My memorial" equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. And it is written, "I am the first and I am the last." <note>Isaiah 44:6</note> He is the absolute perfect; there is no deficiency in Him nor addition. Regarding this comes the warning, "You shall not do so to the Lord your God," <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note> a warning against erasing the Name or smashing a stone from the Temple. The letters of the Name are in the house where He, may He be blessed, dwells; and likewise the Temple. It is written, "I am the Lord, My name is..." The letters are like a closure for the house, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul for them. He who destroys His house, so to speak, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." Service refers to most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place, and he came to the Chosen House, and he said a word with reason: "To His habitation you shall seek, and you shall come there." <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note> "To His habitation" hints at the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the name <term>Yod-Vav</term>, as it is written, "And He descended upon Mount Sinai" <note>Exodus 19:20</note>, and as it is written, "Do not fear, for it will dwell with me," for in the Temple the Glory is unified in the splendor of His people. This is "To His name, His name there," as the <term>Targum</term> <gloss>Aramaic translation</gloss> says: "To cause His <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss> to dwell." And around the place of holiness, the wicked walk, for they are the <term>Kelipah</term> <gloss>shell/force of impurity</gloss>. Therefore, "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in any place that you see." <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>

### **And sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborns of the offering from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written regarding them, "There you shall offer," <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note> meaning, there they shall have an ascent, and not outside. Since the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, is where the holiness is, we were commanded to be "turn from evil" <note>Psalm 34:15</note> by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate after them, and this is commanded specifically in the Holy Land. Its secret hints at the ten nations whose power is not that of idolaters. The matter is that the nations who are in the Land of Israel, under the dominion of the Honored Name, worship the Name by "cutting the shoots" <note>A metaphor for heresy or undermining the divine unity</note>, and this is true idolatry. However, those in the lands outside the Land of Israel are under the dominion of the external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against smashing one stone from the holiness, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and annihilate an "apostate city" <note>Deuteronomy 13:13</note> and not to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Likewise, a seducer and enticer must be uprooted and eradicated, for he is from the impurity of the primordial serpent who was a seducer. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of the seducer are not revived. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, as the matter said regarding the serpent, "And I will put enmity between you and the woman." <note>Genesis 3:15</note> Also, a false prophet is like a seducer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the first fruits, that the priests have no permission to eat them until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first fruits, which are the beginning, indicate great holiness, as I have written elsewhere. Therefore, they shall go to the holy place, and from there they shall take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they shall eat in Jerusalem. The secret of "lesser holy things" and the "second tithe" is that their eating is in Jerusalem. This is the grain, the wine, and the oil, which are the fathers of the fathers of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat lesser holy things until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul. Afterward, there is permission to enjoy. Know that just as the service, which is the offering, is an offering to the Lord, so is the servant, for the essence of the service is that he offers himself, in the secret of "When a man among you offers." <note>Leviticus 1:2</note> And the burnt offering is entirely consumed, for it comes regarding the thought of "turn from evil," the thought which is spiritual, and he is occupied all the night, etc., the serpent does not hinder him. And the lesser holy things are the perfection of the soul and the body.

### **And the secret** of the firstborn is the secret of the holy people of Israel, who are called, as it is written, "Israel is My firstborn." <note>Exodus 4:22</note> He has compassion on them, "And you shall guard them," and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." <note>Psalm 79:13</note> Therefore, it is eaten only by the priests. The secret of eating holy things corresponds to the blemishes and defects in them, for the holy people of Israel are called "man," and he was a holy entity. Afterward, a blemish fell upon him after he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin." <note>Genesis 3:21</note> But he has a redemption, in the secret of "And I will give a man in your stead." <note>Isaiah 43:3</note> This was the secret of <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>the scapegoat</gloss>, "And he shall bear their iniquities." <note>Leviticus 16:22</note> Their iniquities are that they fall upon his head and upon his people. But we were commanded not to cause a blemish in the holy things in order to eat them, for he who causes a blemish in the holy things by his own choice, there is also a prohibition of work and shearing in the holy things, for even the broken tablets are holy.

### **The sum** of the matter is that the service is the offering, but the internal offering is the man. And likewise, his soul is called after his death to the altar above, and Michael is the High Priest. The matter is the secret that "in the image of God He created man." <note>Genesis 1:27</note> Therefore, the warning came to be careful in his life regarding the taking of lives, not to kill a man except after thorough inquiry and investigation. Then it is "pure in the hands of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the witness and He is the judge," for the Lord, may He be blessed, is a true witness and a true judge. So must the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <gloss>High Court</gloss> be; just as they are true judges, so must they be true witnesses. I mean that they must have the clarification of the truth of the witnesses in complete clarity, which is the inquiry and investigation. Then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven, and "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death." <note>Psalm 116:15</note>

### **And since** "precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death," for the holy people of Israel are holy from the side of their souls, which after their death the souls cleave above, therefore the command came: "You shall not cut yourselves, you shall not make a baldness," etc., <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> "for you are children to the Lord your God." <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> This is not so for the nations; the cutting and the baldness are from their customs, for it is appropriate since in their death they go to perdition and they have no portion in this world nor in the world to come. This is not so for us, the children of the Living God. And when one departs from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, or rather, we have a permanent dwelling above with our Father in Heaven, therefore it is forbidden to increase in mourning and to perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter, for the man who serves is himself the offering, as it is written, "When a man among you offers." <note>Leviticus 1:2</note> And there is another secret in this, for the creatures that were created, even below, the man, that is, in the secret of the transmigration, "Man and beast You shall save, O Lord." <note>Psalm 36:7</note> Therefore, even in the eating of ordinary meat, the meat of desire, we were commanded in the slaughtering and in great care without a notch, for then it is a carcass, and then it becomes a carcass in Israel. For who knows what transmigration is in it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>—choose for him a beautiful death, that is, slaughtering without a notch. And if the beast died by itself, or it spread and the power of impurity grasped it, but when he slaughters it properly, and there is in the beast, its sacrifice, and like a pure bird, a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **And he who eats** a limb from a living creature is like one who eats from the flesh of "that one" <note>A euphemism for the demonic/impure</note> when there is a transmigration of a soul there. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh." <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note> And likewise the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of the pure beast, animal, and bird, all indicate the spark that spreads in them, whether it is from the side of the impure or from the side of the holy. I have elaborated on this in the portion of <term>Shemini</term> <gloss>Eighth</gloss>. And Israel, when they conduct themselves in holiness, it is written about them, "And they shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst," <note>Exodus 25:8</note> for they themselves are the tabernacle. For here the man is like three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Holy, and then from the belly downward corresponds to the Courtyard of the Holy, as I have elaborated in the portion of <term>Terumah</term> <gloss>Contribution</gloss>. And when he eats foods that are from the side of the holy, then they are like an offering offered upon the altar. Regarding this, our Sages of blessed memory said: "Now the table of a man atones," as I have elaborated in its place.

### **And the matter** of the commandment of the festivals and their offerings, I have written the matters of each one in its special place. And the command came to rejoice on the festivals and to ascend for the festival, "And three times a year every male of yours shall appear." <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note> And do not read it as "to see," but as "to be seen." Therefore, if he wishes to be seen in the Temple, where the Glory dwells, he must be "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden to enter the hall of the wicked, and how will he wish to be seen before Him, may He be blessed? And he brings a burnt offering of appearance, and then he himself is an offering by means of the offering that he offers. And it said, "Three times a year he shall appear"—Isaac, who lived, is a perfect burnt offering.

### On the shame felt from undeserved praise.
## DIAL. XXVI.

> Praise sparingly, for when you praise unjustly
> If you condemn again, it will be a sign of fickleness.

*Sorrow.* I am accused of having praised an unworthy person.

<note>A large ornamental initial L marks the beginning of the response.</note>

*Reason.* You are accused of having praised an unworthy person. That which is evil often arises from a good root. For good and innocent people, such as they are themselves, imagine others to be the same. Hence, they are even more prone to praise; and although I admit that praising an unworthy person is a bad thing, it is nevertheless much worse to disparage one who is undeserving.

*Sorrow.* I have praised an unworthy person.

*Reason.* If you did it knowingly, you are blameworthy; but if unknowingly, you are excusable. It is a lesser evil to be deceived than to deceive. For to be deceived is the fault of another, but to deceive is the crime of the deceiver himself.

*Sorrow.* The praise of another turns into my own infamy.

*Reason.* On the contrary, it is your own fault or ignorance. For just as there is no praise to be gained from another, so there is no infamy.

*Sorrow.* I grieve greatly for having praised an unworthy person.

*Reason.* See to it, therefore, that you do not grieve for that very thing often. Beware of rushing rashly into praising and disparaging. The splendor, however, appears longer than that of the other stars. Why, you ask? Tell me first why the moon receives a light very different from the sun, when it receives it from the sun? Why does it now redden, now grow pale? Why does it have a livid and black color when it is excluded from the sight of the sun? How does nothing prevent them from being stars, even if they are not similar, just as nothing prevents comets from being eternal and of the same lot as the others, even if they do not have a similar face? Furthermore, if you consider the world itself, is it not composed of diverse things? Why is it that the sun always burns in the lion and scorches the lands with heat? Within a very short time, aries † is cultivated, libra sets most slowly, and yet this star and that one are of the same nature, even if one rises in a short time and the other is brought forth for a long time. Do you not see how contrary the elements are to one another? There are heavy and light, cold and hot, moist and dry. The entire harmony of this world consists of discord. You deny that a comet is a star because its form does not correspond to the model, nor is it similar to the others. For you see, that one which returns to its place in the thirtieth year is very similar to this one which revisits its seat within a year. Nature does not provide its work according to one form, but prides itself on variety itself. It made some things more sluggish, others swifter than others. It made some stronger, others more temperate, but some it led out from the crowd so that they might proceed individually and conspicuously, and some it sent into the flock. He is ignorant of the power of nature who does not think it is permitted to do anything except what it does more often. It does not show comets frequently; it attributes to them another place, other times, and motions dissimilar to the others. It wished to honor the magnitude of its work through these, whose face is more beautiful than that you would think them accidental, whether you consider their size or their brightness, which is greater and more burning than the others. Indeed, it has a face that is remarkable and singular, not cast into a narrow and constricted space, but sent forth more freely, and embracing the region of many stars. Aristotle says that comets signify storms and the intemperance of winds and rains. What then? Do you not judge it to be a star because it denounces future things? For it is not a sign of a storm in the way that oil sparkling or mold growing on bread is a sign of future rain, or in the way that it is an indication of a raging sea if sea-coots play on dry land and desert the known marshes, and the heron flies above the high cloud. But it is so in the way that the equinox is a sign of the heat and cold of the turning year. It is like those things which the Chaldeans sing, what a star determines as sad or happy for those being born. So that you may know this is so, a comet does not immediately threaten winds and rains when it rises, as Aristotle says, but <margin>The rising of a comet makes the whole year suspect.</margin> it makes the whole year suspect. From which it appears that it did not draw the signs it gave for the near future from the near future, but has them stored and compressed by the laws of the world. **And he answered.** "These are the four winds." Like the seven spirits. And so, "And he came to Jerusalem" <note>referring to the grammatical prefix "lamed" used for direction</note> is like "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: "to the seven" <note>referring to the letter "lamed" as a prefix</note> is like "the black son" <note>interpreting the prefix as a signifier of the object</note>. And those similar to it. "To the seven" <note>referring to the division of the four chariots</note> the four chariots go out to the seven winds <note>referring to the verse in 2 Samuel 10</note> of the heavens. All this is to give permission to the seven kingdoms to rule in the seven winds, each one in its time. All this is in the whole world, which is the seven of strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth." All this is in the mission of God, who gave them dominion over this. As it is written, "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin> **In which.** The black ones. And he mentioned the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, for they were in all to destroy it, and after that they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. And the white ones, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them, for the kingdom was bright. For Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him and reigned, and after that, the Persians and the Medes followed him in all the world. **And the dappled ones went out to the south country.** Which were a holy part, as it passed, for Rome is different, and Julius Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece, and at the beginning of his wars he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern, and in all the lands the sons of Greece were ruling. And Julius Caesar overcame them, and he transferred the kingdom from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans. **And the strong ones.** They are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael, which exerted itself to seek a kingdom to live in a place that would be a resting place for them, a spirit for them. And this is what he said, "And they sought to go to walk to and fro in the earth." **And he said.** Meaning, he gave them permission to walk to and fro and to conquer lands. **Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me in a loud voice and said to me, "See, those that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country." Meaning, the portion of the black ones that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

Phlebotomy <note>bloodletting</note> is the specific evacuation for blood. As for evacuation specific to a humor that has increased in quantity or corrupted in quality, it is not phlebotomy. Every evacuation that is excessive causes fainting in most cases. If the cessation of diarrhea causes a habitual ailment, it is often because that evacuation is being repeated, such as when the cessation of a nosebleed causes blockages; thus, returning to it removes them. Know that the remainder of the material that needs to be evacuated is less susceptible to being completely removed, and pushing it to the point of exhausting the strength is often when nature dissolves that remainder. As long as the humor is of the type that is appropriate and the patient can bear it, do not fear excess. You may sometimes need to purge until fainting occurs. Whoever has strong strength and a large amount of corrupt humors should be purged little by little. This occurs in cases of sciatica, chronic joint pain, cancer, chronic scabies, and chronic boils. It is also consistent after the materials have settled; if the materials are from below, the opposite draws them to it and clears them from where they are, and this is by the act of attraction and vice versa. The state of phlebotomy varies according to the places from which the blood is taken, as you have learned. We say: It is recommended for one who wishes to be purged to consume or space out their food in a fixed manner, and the first amount of the dose they test in a day should be in portions, and they should make them different foods and different drinks. For the stomach is affected by this state, such that it desires to push what is in it upward or downward. As for food that is not varied, but rather one food after another, the stomach becomes satisfied with it, relaxes, and grips it tightly, especially if it is small in quantity. As for those with a natural laxative constitution, none of this is necessary. Know that the need for vomiting, diarrhea, and the like does not occur in one who has a good regimen; they need what is lighter than that. Perhaps exercise, massage, and cupping will suffice for them. Then, if their body is filled with the greatest amount of the best humors, meaning blood, then phlebotomy is what is needed for purification, not diarrhea. If necessity dictates phlebotomy or evacuation, such as in autumn, and one is to be purged by vomiting, it is better to do so by phlebotomy. This is one of the recommendations of Hippocrates and the books that follow it, and it is the truth. Likewise, if the phlegmatic humors are mixed with blood. And if the humors are equal, viscous, and cold, phlebotomy might increase their thickness and viscosity, so it is necessary to begin with diarrhea. In general, if the humors are equal, prioritize phlebotomy; if a purge is needed after that, then purge. If they are not equal, purge the excess first until they are equal, then perform phlebotomy. Whoever prioritizes medicine over phlebotomy should have prioritized phlebotomy, even if only a little. Whoever was recently phlebotomized and needed to purge, and drank the medicine, it was stopped for them. Often, drinking the medicine when phlebotomy was required resulted in fainting and agitation. If it does not subside with sedatives, then phlebotomy should have been prioritized. There is no evacuation needed due to excessive fullness that is not called for by the severity of the ailment and the fullness according to quality and quantity. Often, good regimen replaces the necessary phlebotomy at the time. Often, the need for evacuation arises, but an obstacle opposes it, so the only solution is fasting, sleep, and correcting the dyscrasia <note>imbalance of humors</note> by way of fullness. Some evacuation is by way of precaution, such as what is needed for those accustomed to gout, epilepsy, or other things at a known time, especially in the spring. It is necessary to take precautions before its time and perform the specific evacuation, whether it is phlebotomy or diarrhea. Sometimes the use of external drying agents and desiccating medicines is a form of evacuation, as is done with those suffering from dropsy. You may be forced to use a medicine that is homogeneous to the humor being purged in quality, such as scammony when you need to purge yellow bile. It is then necessary to mix with it something that differs in quality but agrees in purging, such as myrobalan. Correcting the dyscrasia if it occurs afterward in those with visceral tumors weakens their diarrhea. If you are forced to do that, use for them things like ivy and safflower. As for the purgative and cassia fistula, this is what Hippocrates said: whoever has a constitution that easily responds to vomiting, the first step in their purification is to use vomiting in summer or spring when it is time, for that relieves the body of fatigue. Know that the one who is accustomed to a laxative constitution or is not accustomed to vomiting in the summer should avoid it when there is no need. It is necessary to prepare before diarrhea by softening the humor one wishes to purge and widening the passages at that time, for that relieves the body of fatigue. Know that the one who is accustomed to a laxative constitution or is not accustomed to vomiting before using strong medicine should use one of the regimens of reduction. Diarrhea with abdominal emaciation is difficult and tiring. A purgative medicine may return to being a laxative if the stomach is strong, or if it is taken during intense hunger, or if the person is accustomed to a laxative constitution, or because of the medicine, or if the medicine is heavier in substance than the quick-acting ones. A purgative may become a cause of nausea due to the weakness of the stomach, or the intensity of the heaviness, or because the medicine irritates it, or because the person has indigestion. Every purgative medicine, if it does not purge the undigested matter, stirs up the humor it is meant to purge and spreads it in the body, so it takes hold of the body and draws other humors to it, increasing that humor in the body. Some humors are more responsive to vomiting in most cases, such as yellow bile. Some are resistant to vomiting, such as black bile. Some have a state like milk and stars <note>likely a reference to specific herbal preparations or celestial timing</note>, and its diarrhea is more correct in itself. Whoever has a humor that is descending, such as those with intestinal slippage, the gripping of the intestines hinders the purgative medicine. What is composed of medicines that are highly different in the time of diarrhea causes the diarrhea to be agitated, and the first purges the second before the second purges, and perhaps the first purges the second itself. Whoever is exposed to diarrhea and their body is not cleansed of it must have a medicine for colic and the distress that accompanies it, and what is evacuated is evacuated with great difficulty. In general, the medicine that evacuates the superfluities does not cause agitation with it. If it is taken with agitation, it either evacuates what is not a superfluity, or if the evacuated humor changes by vomiting or diarrhea to another humor, it indicates the cleansing of the body from the humor intended to be purged.

But have we not learned in a <term>Mishnah</term> <gloss>the foundational text of the Oral Law</gloss>: All handles of foodstuffs that are in the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yose declares them impure. It is well for the one who says "in the threshing floor" <term>bagoren</term> <gloss>in the threshing floor</gloss>—as it was taught, "their bundles"—this is well. But for the one who says "what is 'in the threshing floor'?"—it means literally in the threshing floor—what is there to say? Here too, it is literally in the threshing floor. If so, what is the reasoning of the Rabbis who say [it is pure]? It is as Rabbi Yose says, for we learned: Rabbi Yose declares them impure. But what is this? It is well there, for the reasoning of Rabbi Yose is that of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who said: Since they are fit to turn them with a pitchfork. But here, for what are they fit? Is it to say to gather them in their stalks? The body [of the text]: All handles of foodstuffs that are in the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yose [declares them impure]. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: What is "in the threshing floor"? Rabbi Yochanan said: Literally in the threshing floor. Rabbi Eliezer says: The permission of their gathering—that it is literally in the threshing floor—Rabbi Eliezer, who said "in the threshing floor" is the permission of their gathering, that is why Rabbi Yose declares them impure. But Rabbi Eliezer: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork? To tell you: Just as this pitchfork turns the grain in the threshing floor from place to place, so too the prayer of the righteous turns the mind of the Holy One, blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

What, therefore, is the manner in which God foreknows these uncertain future events? For if He deems that things are avoidable in the future, when it is not possible for them to happen, He is deceived; and to think this is not only wicked, but even to utter it. But if He discerns that they are to be future in such a way that He knows they can either happen or not happen, what kind of foreknowledge is this, which grasps nothing certain and nothing stable? Or how does this differ from that ridiculous prophecy of Tiresias, who said, "Whatever I shall say, it will either be or it will not be"? Why, then, should divine providence differ from human opinion, if it judges uncertain things just as men do, whose outcome is uncertain? But if, in that most certain fountain of all things, nothing uncertain...

<summary>Boethius questions how divine foreknowledge can exist if future events are uncertain, arguing that if God perceives events as merely possible rather than necessary, His knowledge lacks stability and resembles human conjecture.</summary>

The third article is proceeded with thus: that more universal things are not prior in our intellectual cognition. Because those things which are prior according to nature are posterior and less known according to us, but universals are prior according to the nature of our intellect. Furthermore, composite things are prior with respect to us than simple things, but universals are prior <unclear>in nature</unclear>; they are posterior in knowledge with respect to us. Furthermore, the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> says in the first book of the *Physics* that the defined falls into our cognition before the parts of the definition, and the parts of the definition are less universal: just as "animal" is a part of the definition of "human," and universals are known later with respect to us. Furthermore, effects are known before causes and principles, but universals are known later with respect to us. But if it is as the Philosopher says in the first book of the *Physics*, we must arrive from singulars to universals. I answer that it must be said that in the cognition of our intellect two things must be considered. First, that intellectual cognition in some way takes its beginning from sensitive cognition. And because sense is of singulars, and intellect is of universals, it is necessary that the cognition of singulars be prior with respect to us than the cognition of universals. Second, it must be considered that our intellect proceeds from potency to act. And that which proceeds from potency to act arrives first at an incomplete act, which is intermediate between potency and perfect act. The perfect act to which the intellect arrives is complete science, through which things are known distinctly and determinately; the incomplete act is imperfect science, through which things are known indistinctly under a certain confusion. For that which is known in this way is known in act and in a certain way in potency. As the Philosopher says in the first book of the *Physics*: things are first manifest and certain to us in a more confused way; later, however, we know by distinguishing the principles and elements distinctly. It is manifest, however, that to know something in which many things are contained without having proper knowledge of each of those things contained in it is to know something under a certain confusion. In this way, however, both the whole in which parts are contained in potency and the integral whole can be known; for each whole can be known in a certain confusion without the parts being known distinctly. To know distinctly that which is contained in the whole, however, is to have knowledge of a less common thing: just as to know "animal" indistinctly, and to know the animal in which there is rational or irrational, which is to know a human or a lion. Therefore, it occurs to our intellect first to know "animal" and then to know "human." And if I compare any thing to the more or less, just as sense goes from potency to act, so does the intellect; this is the order

<column-break/>

of cognition that appears in sense. For in sense, one judges more and when less is known, it is more remote through <unclear>the being of a body</unclear>, and <unclear>it is a body</unclear> and an animal; and more <unclear>is perceived</unclear> the being an animal and <unclear>it is a body</unclear> and <unclear>the good</unclear> and prior <unclear>the good</unclear> and <unclear>the sort</unclear>. Or it pleases and it is clear that a child from the beginning distinguishes <unclear>the good</unclear> and <unclear>from the good</unclear>; and in children from the beginning they call all men "father." Later, however, he terminates each one, as the Philosopher says in the first book of the *Physics*: things are manifest and one knows something indistinctly still and in potency, or one knows <unclear>the fiction</unclear> and the principle, thus one knows <unclear>the genus</unclear> and is able to know the <unclear>species</unclear>. And thus, by itself, indistinct cognition is intermediate between potency and act. And that the cognition of singulars is prior with respect to us, and the cognition of the universal is [posterior to] sensitive cognition and intellectual cognition. If both sense and intellect [are considered], the cognition of the less [universal] and common is prior. To the first, it must be said that it can be considered in a twofold way. One way is that which is considered thus according to the intention of truth. And since the intention of truth and the true is the same, it has a relationship to many things. It arrives at the abstraction of the intellect, and this is the end, while the true is posterior. In the first book of *De Anima*, the universal is either nothing or it is posterior; but <unclear>Plato</unclear> posited universals as substances; and in this consideration it is true, more because particulars are not except by participation in the more universal subsisting things which are called ideas. In another way, it can be considered with respect to the nature itself of animality or humanity as it is found in particulars. And thus there is a twofold order of nature. One is according to the way of generation and time, when those things which are imperfect and in potency are prior. And in this way, the more universal is posterior in nature, which appears manifestly in the generation of a human and an animal. For an animal is generated before a human, as the Philosopher says in the book *On the Generation of Animals*. Another is the order of perfection or the intention of nature, just as act is simply prior in nature to that which is in potency, and that which is perfect is prior to that which is imperfect; and in this way, the less universal is prior in nature, for the intention of nature does not rest in the generation of an animal, but it intends to generate a human. To the second, the more universal is compared to the less universal as a whole, and through the whole it becomes more universal, not only <unclear>the common</unclear> but also human and horse; as it can be [that] the less universal is contained in the future, not only the more universal but also others, as human is not only animal but rational. Thus, therefore, animal considered in itself is prior in our cognition than human. If human is prior in our cognition, then animal is [known] through the reason of it. To the third, it must be said that something can be known in two ways. In one way, absolutely, according to what it is in itself, and thus nothing is <unclear>a house</unclear>. In another way, when it is a part of this whole, and stones, it is necessary that we know the whole before the parts. For we know the house in a certain confused way; thus, therefore, it must be said that the definition to be considered absolutely is prior to the defined. Otherwise, the defined would not be notified by those things. But rather, they are the parts.

Kalila and Dimna

<note>A decorative floral-style border frames the top and bottom of the page.</note>

When the Lion awoke the next morning, the judge entered with a group of prominent companions, carrying the document containing the excuses Dimna had provided. The Lion took the document and ordered them to leave him.

He then sent for his mother and read the document to her. It distressed her, and she said, "If I speak harshly to you, O King, do not be angry."

The Lion replied, "I will not be angry, so say what you wish."

She said, "I do not see that you distinguish between what harms you and what benefits you. I fear that by continuing to deliberate on Dimna’s case, you will stir up a situation you cannot withstand or overcome."

She then stood up and left in anger. The next day, the judge sent for Dimna and brought him out. He consulted the scholars regarding him, but they said nothing.

The judge said to him, "Even if everyone present remains silent and says nothing, their suspicions have converged on the fact that you are a criminal. There is no good for you in life once the accusation has settled in their hearts. I see nothing better for you than to confess your guilt. This will free your neck from the consequences in the hereafter, and a good reputation may return to you for two reasons: first, your ability to provide explanations and fabricate excuses that defend yourself; and second, your voluntary confession of guilt, choosing safety in the hereafter over safety in this world. For the scholars have said: 'Death in a manner that is honorable is better than life in a manner that is disgraceful.'"

Dimna answered him, saying, "Judges do not pass judgment based on their own suspicions, nor the suspicions of the common people, nor the elite. You know that suspicion does not replace the truth in any way. Even if you all suspect that I am the perpetrator of this crime, I have knowledge of myself, and my knowledge of myself is a certainty in which there is no doubt. My situation has only become ugly in your eyes—if that is indeed the case—because you suspected that I strove..."

<summary>The Lion’s mother warns him against further leniency toward Dimna, while the judge pressures Dimna to confess his crimes to secure a better fate in the afterlife.</summary>

The strange thing is that there is a girl like the moon, soft and delicate like fur and fine silk.
She carries a cow, like a mountain, upon her neck to the place where it eats grass.

**The Second Affliction:** This arises from a friend of Islam who is ignorant. He thought that religion should be defended by denying every science attributed to them. So, he denied all their sciences and claimed they were ignorant in them, even denying their statements regarding solar and lunar eclipses, claiming that what they said was contrary to religious law. 3222. Furthermore, loves and their affections are represented by flames, and this with an inexpressible variation. Truths, however, are represented by lights and by the innumerable modifications of light. From this it can be evident why, in the Word, flames signify the goods that belong to love, and lights signify the truths that belong to faith.

3223. There are two lights by which man is illuminated: the light of the world and the light of heaven. The light of the world is from the sun; the light of heaven is from the Lord. The light of the world is for the natural or external man, and thus for those things that are within him. The things that are there, even though they do not appear to be of that light, still are, for nothing can be grasped by the natural man except through such things as exist and appear in the solar world, and thus they have some form only by the light and shadow there. All ideas of time and ideas of space, which in the natural man are so essential that he cannot think without them, also belong to the light of the world. The light of heaven, however, is for the spiritual or internal man. The interior mind of man, where his intellectual ideas—which are called immaterial—reside, is in that light. Man does not know this, even though he calls his intellect "sight" and attributes light to it. The reason is that, as long as he is in worldly and bodily things, he has only a perception of such things as belong to the light of the world, and not of such things as belong to the light of heaven. The light of heaven is from the Lord alone; the entire heaven is in that light. This light, namely the light of heaven, is immensely more perfect than the light of the world. Those things that in the light of the world make one ray, in the light of heaven make myriads. In the light of heaven there is intelligence and wisdom. That light is what flows into the light of the world which is in the external or natural man, and causes him to perceive the objects of things sensually. Unless that light flowed in, man would have no apperception at all, for those things that belong to the light of the world have life from that source. Between these lights, or between those things that are in the light of heaven and in the light of the world, there is a correspondence when the external or natural man makes one with the internal or spiritual man—that is, when the former serves the latter. And the things that then exist in the light of the world are representative of such things as are in the light of heaven.

3224. It is remarkable that man does not yet know that his intellectual mind is in a certain light which is entirely different from the light of the world. Those who are in the loves of self and of the world, and thus in the heat of the light of the world alone, are affected only by evils and falsities, and these are what extinguish the truths that are of the light of heaven. # We have set the distance

from noon because the adjustment for the birth <note>referring to the astronomical new moon or conjunction</note> is easier than working with horizons and the longest daylight hours for the latitude of Jerusalem, which is fourteen hours and some fraction. Therefore, the Jewish method of working with temporal hours <note>unequal hours that vary by season</note> is not valid unless the conjunction for the beginning of Tishrei <note>the first month of the Jewish civil year</note> occurs at the autumnal equinox. It never occurs with it, but rather precedes or follows it by a significant amount, as we have explained previously. Once we have derived the time of the conjunction using the calculation that the Jews provided in the table we analyzed according to their view, we progress from that to the knowledge of the beginning of the year and the understanding of its nature regarding deficiency, moderation, and fullness. We have already gained knowledge of whether it is a common or a leap year. We then look in the table of limits for a duration of days of the week whose boundaries contain the time at which the conjunction occurred for us, in the section for leap years if it is a leap year, and in the section for common years if it is a common year. When we find it, we find alongside it the beginning of the year from the week and its nature. When we know the beginning of the year and its nature, and we combine that nature with the common or leap year, we know from that the passage of the beginning of the next year.

Entering into meditative equipoise, the state in which one does not provide an opportunity for afflictions to arise in the mental continuum of others through the power of previous aspirations is called the meditative equipoise of being without afflictions. Because one has made that aspiration, the wisdom that immediately realizes those phenomena is called wisdom preceded by aspiration, or "aspirational wisdom."

Regarding the question, "What are the four purities?", they are as follows: The complete separation of all sentient beings from the latent predispositions of afflictions, the ability to assume one's own body as one desires, and the mastery over abiding and passing away <note>death and rebirth</note> constitute the purity of place. The mastery over emanations, the various transformations, and all objects of focus constitutes the purity of focus. The increase of virtue in all aspects of the mind due to being free from all the latent predispositions of the mind constitutes the purity of mind. The unobstructed mastery of wisdom over all that is to be known, due to being free from all latent predispositions on the side of ignorance, constitutes the purity of primordial wisdom.

Regarding the question, "What are the ten masteries?", they are as follows: Remaining for as long as one desires is mastery over life. Abiding in meditative concentration, immeasurable states, liberations, and so forth, exactly as one wishes to abide, is mastery over mind.
